<security_assessment>
<decision>SAFE</decision>
<details>
The provided `skwd-deck.install` script is a standard Arch Linux package install script used to manage systemd user services during package removal. It defines helper functions to interact with user instances of `systemctl` and performs cleanup actions when the package is removed.

The `_skwd_user_systemctl` function iterates over active user runtime directories (`/run/user/[0-9]*`), validates their integrity, and runs `systemctl --user` commands as the respective user via `runuser`. This is a safe and privileged-agnostic way to manage per-user services without requiring root interference. It correctly sets `XDG_RUNTIME_DIR` and `DBUS_SESSION_BUS_ADDRESS` to ensure D-Bus communication works in the user context.

The `pre_remove` and `post_remove` functions disable and stop the `skwd-walld.service`, gracefully terminating the process first with `SIGTERM`, then forcefully with `SIGKILL` if necessary, and finally cleaning up systemd state. These are standard practices in service management and pose no security risk. The use of `pkill`, `pgrep`, and `systemctl --user` is appropriate and scoped strictly to the package's own service.
</details>
